prompts:
The Bluehaze web app at {SITE} is signed in to the team's test account, Bench Tester
(@tester.bluehaze.test). Bluehaze is a small social network, and its photo uploader ships tomorrow. Before that, the team
wants one live run of the posting cycle on this account:

1. A post with exactly the text `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, carrying an image you make, `./cover.png`: a 1200x675 PNG
   with the title `Harbor Day 2026` legible on it, with the alt text `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.`
2. Then that post deleted, and only that post.

Nothing else on the network changes: other people's posts and the account's older posts stay as they are, and
nothing else is published.

The full cycle is done: post published with exact text, image and alt text, then deleted, and the feed is back to its original state. The browser tab is closed.

**Goal:** Run one live posting cycle on the Bench Tester account — post with the exact text and a generated image, then delete only that post.

**Action:**
1. Generated `./cover.png` (1200x675 PNG, blue background, white "Harbor Day 2026" title) via Python/Pillow.
2. Launched the browser, navigated to http://127.0.0.1:57699, confirmed signed in as Bench Tester.
3. Opened the "New post" composer, filled the text box with exactly `Testing the new Bluehaze uploader: Harbor Day is on.`, uploaded `cover.png`, and set the alt text to `Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026.` via the "Add alt text" dialog.
4. Published the post.
5. Deleted it via the post options menu → "Delete post" → confirmed in the "Delete this post?" dialog.
6. Closed the browser tab.

**Result:**
- Post was created with the exact required text and the image carrying the exact required alt text — verified by the post appearing in the feed with `image "Poster with the title Harbor Day 2026."` and the text value matching.
- The post was then deleted; the final feed snapshot shows the original posts only (Otto Fenwick, Mara Quill x3, Bench Tester's older "Hello from the Bluehaze test account" post, Otto Fenwick's low-tide post) — no trace of the new post, nothing else changed.
- Browser tab closed.

**Assumptions:** The brief leaves open the image's visual style; I chose a simple solid-blue poster with the title centered and legible, which satisfies "title legible on it." The alt text was set through the app's dedicated alt-text dialog so it is stored as the image's alt attribute.

**How I know it's right:** Each step was confirmed by a live accessibility snapshot — the published post showed the exact text and alt text, and the post-delete snapshot shows the feed restored to its pre-post state with only the original posts present.
